page: Microsoft Azure F64-32amds_v7 is a compute-focused instance configured with constrained core counts to offer an elevated memory-to-vCPU ratio. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, it features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The underlying AMD processor provides 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, along with extended instruction sets including AVX-512 (F, VNNI, BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI.

Despite belonging to the compute-optimized lineage, this configuration bundles 512.0 GB of total RAM, delivering 16.0 GB of memory per core. Storage is also fully provisioned locally with 7,560 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD capacity. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks highlight exceptional memory and storage throughput, scoring in the top tier for PassMark memory (3,029.38) and PassMark database operations (37,989.46), alongside a strong uncached read bandwidth of 219.58 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 135.09 GB/sec.

In compute workloads, the instance achieves top-tier single-core stress-ng performance (3,642.79) and single-threaded compression throughput (39.65 GB/sec for gzip and 17.84 GB/sec for bzip3). Multi-core throughput is strong, marked by a multi-core stress-ng score of 116,567.07 and 93.4 million Redis SET operations per second. CPU-based small LLM inference runs exceptionally fast at 5,006.15 prompt tokens per second, though larger models like 70B show average CPU throughput (3.01 generation tokens per second) due to the absence of dedicated matrix accelerators.

The F64-32amds_v7 represents an efficient hardware balance when software licensing is constrained by core counts, providing full access to 512 GB of RAM and 7.5 TB of NVMe SSD without paying per-core software premiums for an unneeded 64 cores. It is ideally positioned for in-memory databases, large cache layers, heavy database operations, data ingestion pipelines, and compute tasks requiring generous local scratch storage.

While lacking hardware GPU accelerators, the instance incorporates AVX-512 instructions, AES cryptography, and substantial cache hierarchies. Benchmark performance places it in the top tier for single-core stress-ng tests, PassMark memory scores, and database operation benchmarks, while uncached memory bandwidth reaches 219.58 GB/sec read and 135.09 GB/sec write.
